newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper concedes economy is weak.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper concedes economy is weak.

text.p: President Ernesto Samper conceded Tuesday that Colombia's economy was in the midst of a sharp slowdown. But he urged the business community to "keep the faith" and said the country was still a long way from catastrophe.
"The year 1996 will certaintly not be a good one economically, but its results won't be catastrophic either," Samper said.

The embattled Samper has endured repeated calls from leading businessmen and industrialists to step down because the year-old crisis stemming from charges his 1994 election campaign was partly financed by drug lords.
The crisis and political uncertainty have been cited as among the leading causes of a precipitous drop in industrial production and sales so far this year.

But Samper, who spoke at the swearing-in ceremony of his new vice president, blamed slowing growth rates on a host of other factors including what he called the "ethical adjustment" Colombia has had to make in the aftermath of its crackdown on the powerful Cali drug cartel.
The crackdown has been partly blamed for a deep slump in the construction sector, which Cali kingpins reportedly used to launder vast sums of illicit drug money.
The government has rolled back its estimates of growth in the gross domestic product this year to 3.5 percent from an original target of more than 5.0 percent.

In his speech, Samper said this was still "acceptable compared with other economies of the area." And he stressed that despite his many adversaries in the business community "the government expects an act of faith from businessmen in the possibilities our econonmy has to recover."
